original_question: Is the isomorphism problem for 2-knot groups algorithmically unsolvable? In other words, is there no algorithm that takes finite presentations of two groups known to belong to K_2, the class of groups of 2-knots, and always decides whether the two groups are isomorphic?
target_in_paper: Introduction (§1), the unnumbered sentence immediately after the discussion of Theorem 1.1: "Conjecturally this should hold also for K_2," where "this" refers to the preceding sentence that the isomorphism problem is unsolvable for K_3 and the larger classes containing it. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/44199))
correct_elements: Your draft already targets the right issue: the isomorphism problem for 2-knot groups; it uses the correct input model (finite presentations), assumes the inputs are known to define groups in K_2, and asks about algorithmic decidability of group isomorphism. That matches the paper’s conjectural extension of its K_3 result to K_2. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/44199))
missing_details: The paper presents this only conjecturally, not as a proved theorem. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/44199))

K_2 should be defined explicitly as the class of fundamental groups of complements of locally flat PL embeddings S^2 into S^4, i.e. PL 2-knots. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/44199))

The official wording is tied to Theorem 1.1 and, in particular, to the case (A,B)=(K_3,K_0), where K_0 is the class consisting only of the infinite cyclic group; that context is implicit in your draft. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/44199))

For the decision problem to be well-posed in the paper’s framework, one also needs that P(K_2), the set of finite presentations of groups in K_2, is recursively enumerable. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/44199))

The paper separately records related but distinct open questions—whether there exists a 2-knot group with unsolvable word problem, and whether every finitely presented group embeds in a 2-knot group—and these should not replace the isomorphism-problem question itself. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/44199))
refined_question: Is the isomorphism problem algorithmically unsolvable for K_2, the class of fundamental groups of complements of locally flat PL 2-knots S^2 into S^4? In other words, is there no algorithm that, given finite presentations of two groups known a priori to lie in K_2, always decides whether those two groups are isomorphic? ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/44199))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. The paper does not state a numbered conjecture specifically for K_2-isomorphism; instead, after Theorem 1.1 it says that the isomorphism problem is unsolvable for K_3 and the three larger classes containing it, and then adds that this should conjecturally also hold for K_2. The refined question therefore keeps the scope exactly at K_2 isomorphism, while adding the paper’s definition of K_2 and the recursive-enumerability context needed for a self-contained algorithmic statement. I did not replace it by the neighboring concluding questions about unsolvable word problem or universal embedding in 2-knot groups, because those are related motivations but not the same problem. ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/44199))
